facts: Automated facial expression recognition has received increased attention over the past two decades.
Existing works usually do not encode the temporal evolution of the observed facial displays.
Existing works usually do not encode the intensity of the observed facial displays.
Existing works fail to jointly model multidimensional (multi-class) continuous facial behaviour data.
Existing works use binary classifiers, one for each target basic-emotion class.
The intrinsic topology of multidimensional continuous facial affect data is first modeled by an ordinal manifold.
The ordinal manifold topology is incorporated into the Hidden Conditional Ordinal Random Field (H-CORF) framework for dynamic ordinal regression.
The Hidden Conditional Ordinal Random Field (H-CORF) is a framework.
The Hidden Conditional Ordinal Random Field (H-CORF) framework is for dynamic ordinal regression.
H-CORF parameters are constrained to lie on the ordinal manifold.
The resulting model attains simultaneous dynamic recognition and intensity estimation of facial expressions of multiple emotions.
The proposed method is the first to achieve simultaneous dynamic recognition and intensity estimation on deliberate facial affect data.
The proposed method is the first to achieve simultaneous dynamic recognition and intensity estimation on spontaneous facial affect data.
Hidden Conditional Ordinal Random Field is abbreviated as H-CORF.
The resulting model addresses facial expressions of multiple emotions.
